title: Leading-context hotstore and GPU compact index for cross-request prompt reuse
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: A significant portion of inference requests share identical or near-identical leading context (system messages, onboarding text, or fixed prompt headers). In current runtime the KV cache stores separate entries for these repeated leading-context tokens and frequently wastes GPU-resident KV slices, increasing memory pressure and causing unnecessary recomputation across requests. This manifests as higher eviction churn and increased tail latency under multi-tenant load.

Goal: Design and implement a compact, GPU-resident index + small host hotstore that enables cross-request reuse of leading-context KV material without requiring full model checkpoint duplication. The system should: (1) detect and fingerprint identical/near-identical leading contexts, (2) map fingerprints to compact slice descriptors that can be shared across requests, (3) allow safe reuse across tenants subject to isolation policies, and (4) integrate with continuous batching to maximize reuse opportunities while preserving latency SLOs.

Proposed solution: Build a two-tier cache: a lightweight host hotstore that maintains canonical fingerprints (64-bit content-addressed signatures) and eviction metadata, plus a compact GPU index that stores mapping entries (fingerprint -> KV-slice descriptor) and reference counts. On request arrival, the scheduler consults the hotstore to resolve the leading-context fingerprint and, if present, emits a reuse directive to the GPU runtime to attach the existing KV slice to the request's execution context instead of materializing a duplicate. To avoid drift and stale references, we will use epoch-based residency tokens and a background compaction pass that coalesces fragmented slices.

Key design points: fingerprinting algorithm choices (BLAKE3 truncated to 64b vs farmhash), probabilistic membership gating (bloom filter) to reduce host lookups, multi-tenant namespace isolation, ephemeral tenancy-scoped reference counts, and a compact GPU index layout optimized for coalesced reads. We will support "approximate" reuse for templated prompts by storing a canonicalization transformation (normalize whitespace/tokens, strip user slots) before fingerprinting.

Metrics & success criteria: target 15-25% reduction in net GPU-resident KV bytes on mixed workloads with high leading-context repetition; expect 6-12% improvement in p99 tail latency for small interactive requests; maintain less than 1% false-positive reuse rate (safety via checksum verification during attach).

Security & safety: reuse must never mix confidential per-tenant context. The hotstore will include tenant tags and reuse will be gated by tenancy policy. All host/GPU transfers of descriptors occur inside existing encrypted control channels; audit logs will record every reuse decision. Security review required before enabling cross-tenant reuse.

Rollout plan: prototype as opt-in flag in runtime-1.22 in a canary cluster for internal traffic. If stable, gradually enable for Dedicated customers with allowlist.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Sync with scheduler team: agreed to add a small fast-path in the scheduler for fingerprint lookup. Miguel to prototype hotstore interface in Go runtime shim.

2026-02-28 - Design review: PM and security raised concerns about accidental cross-tenant data reuse. Decided to enforce tenant tags on fingerprints and disallow cross-tenant matches unless explicit allowlist is set. Added mandatory checksum verification in GPU attach path.

2026-03-03 - Prototype status: host hotstore implemented as an in-memory LRU-backed map with bloom gating. Early microbench against synthetic workload (30% repeated system messages) shows 18% GPU KV memory reduction and 9% lower p99 latency on internal dev cluster.
2026-03-05 - PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8921 - initial hotstore API + GPU index ABI. Requesting runtime team review (cc @elaine-chen, @ryan-wu).

2026-03-08 - Review feedback: Elaine: prefer BLAKE3 truncated-64 instead of farmhash for collision resistance. Ryan: add metrics for reuse hits vs validation failures. Added both changes to PR. Miguel pushed updates.

2026-03-10 - Load test plan approved: run 48h mixed-tenant simulation with realistic PLG traffic (50% templated prompts) and monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU KV bytes, eviction churn, and reuse telemetry. If reuse validation failures > 0.5% or any isolated tenant sees unexpected exposure, abort rollout.
